title: Sort Vowels in a String
statement:
The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o` and `u` in either case; every other letter is a consonant. Rearrange the letters of `s` into a new string `t` of the same length where:

- each consonant stays at exactly the index it had in `s`;
- the vowels fill the remaining indices in non-decreasing order of ASCII code, so whenever `i < j` are both vowel indices, `t[i]` has a code no greater than `t[j]`'s. (Every uppercase letter comes before every lowercase one in ASCII.)

Return `t`.
constraints: s contains only uppercase and lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Consonants never move, so the indices that hold vowels are fixed too: only which vowel lands on each of them changes. Pull the vowels out, sort them, and put them back into the vowel slots from left to right. Sorting the characters directly works because ASCII order is exactly what the problem asks for, with uppercase letters (codes 65–90) before lowercase ones (97–122).

## Approach

1. Scan `s` and push every vowel into `vowels`.
2. Sort `vowels`; JavaScript's default sort compares strings by character code, which matches ASCII for letters.
3. Scan `s` again, building `result`: at a vowel take `vowels[next]` and advance `next`; at a consonant copy the character.
4. Join `result` into the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "lEetcOde"`. The vowels in order are `E`, `e`, `O`, `e`; sorted they become `E`, `O`, `e`, `e` (both capitals first). The second scan copies `l`, places `E` at index 1, `O` at index 2, copies `t`, `c`, places `e` at index 5, copies `d`, and places `e` at index 7, giving `"lEOtcede"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for sorting the vowels (O(n) with a counting sort over the ten vowel letters).
- Space: O(n) for `vowels` and `result`.

## Pitfalls

- Uppercase vowels count as vowels too; check both cases.
- Sort by character code, not alphabetically ignoring case: `"O"` comes before `"e"`.
- Building the answer with repeated string concatenation in Java is quadratic; use a `char[]` or `StringBuilder`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `isVowel` | tells whether a character is one of the ten vowel letters |
| `vowels` | the vowels of `s`, sorted after the first scan |
| `result` | characters of the answer, built in order |
| `next` | index of the next sorted vowel to place |
| `ch` | the character of `s` being looked at |
